meta.title: Roadmap
meta.description: What is planned after the first stable release — as a list of intentions, without dates.

intro: These are the things the package is meant to grow after 1.0. There are no dates on them, and nothing here is a commitment: the order is what makes sense today, and the first release has to come first.

rows: Moving and resizing items by pointer and by keyboard, with items that can be locked against it.
Rendering only what is near the viewport. The budgets are met without it today, which is why it is not in 1.0.
Arrow-key movement between cards, and shortcuts for the navigation buttons.
Rendering a day in a zone other than the reader’s. Today the component is local-zone and DST-safe.
A built-in way to pick the day. The date is the consumer’s to choose today.
Remembering view, scroll position and pinned items across visits, behind a prop.
Letting a capability be added from outside the package instead of behind a flag.

notPlanned.intro: Some things are deliberately outside what this component does, and saying so is part of the roadmap:
points: A data layer. The component never fetches; items are yours, from wherever you keep them.
A state library. The state is React state, controlled or uncontrolled, and nothing else is needed.
A styling runtime. The looks are CSS variables and class names, resolved by the browser.
A calendar. This is a schedule of one day at a time, not a month view or a year view.

how.text: An item moves from this page to the <link to="/discover-more/changelog/">Changelog</link> when it ships, and disappears from here when it is decided against. If something you need is missing, <link to="/getting-started/support/">Support</link> is where to say so.
